geo.label: March lift-off, front end reprices
parts: Macro Stance

Two shocks now push US equity multiples in the same direction. January consumer prices rose 7.5% from a year earlier, the hottest reading since 1982 and more than expected, according to CNBC. [[n2132]] Bloomberg described the gain as larger than forecast. [[n2138]] On Friday the White House added that Russia could invade Ukraine within the week, Stars and Stripes reported. [[n1578]] The S&P 500 fell 1.90% to 4,418.64 index points and the Nasdaq 100 lost 3.07% to 14,253.84 index points, while the VIX jumped 3.45 points to 27.36 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). We are Bearish on duration-heavy US equity: the Fed is being pulled forward just as an exogenous risk premium is being added.
Rates & Curve

The two-year Treasury closed at 1.50% and the ten-year at 1.92%, leaving the 10Y−2Y spread at +42 bps on a positively sloped curve (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11). Over 20 observations the two-year has risen 59 bps from 0.91% while the ten-year is up only 22 bps from 1.70%, so the spread has compressed by 37 bps: a bear flattening, with both yields up and the two-year up more. The last five observations concentrate the move, with the two-year up 19 bps and the ten-year down 1 bp, after the ten-year briefly topped 2% for the first time since 2019 on the inflation print, according to CNBC. [[n2192]] Reuters has published an explainer on why the flattening matters. [[n2198]] The front of the curve is still steep, with 10Y−3M at +156 bps, so the Fed has room to hike before inversion becomes the dominant signal.
New / Most Important

The policy debate has moved from whether to how fast. Reuters reports that hot inflation fuels the case for a 'big-bang' Fed hike in March. [[n2201]] Against that, the Fed's Barkin told Reuters he would have to be convinced of the need for a half-point move. [[n1365]] Households are already absorbing the shock: Yahoo Finance describes US consumers as 'in a deep funk' [[n2147]], and the Orange County Register reports the 30-year mortgage rate has surged to 3.69%, a two-year high. [[n2135]] The dollar index (DXY) rose 0.55% on Friday to 96.08 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), tightening financial conditions further. The geopolitical layer is the new element: a war premium is now competing with the Fed for the same drawdown budget.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ closed at 347.06 USD, down 8.10% over 20 sessions) against the energy sector ETF (XLE, up 11.71% over the same span), and hold seven-to-ten-year Treasuries (IEF, up 1.04% on Friday) as the war hedge rather than adding equity beta (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger to press the trade: the VIX holding above 27.36 index points while the two-year stays at or above 1.50% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11). What changes the call: a verifiable Russian pull-back that sends the VIX back toward its 20-session reference of 20.31 index points, combined with a softer next inflation print, would argue for covering growth underweights before the March meeting.

geo.label: ECB patient as energy risk rises
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is where the Ukraine risk and the inflation problem meet, and the ECB is not yet offering a backstop. Reuters argues the ECB 'put' for euro zone bond markets is some way off. [[n1306]] Germany's Scholz has warned Moscow of immediate sanctions if Ukraine is attacked, per Reuters [[n1499]], and DW describes his diplomacy as a delicate mission. [[n1342]] We are Bearish on euro-area equities relative to the UK.
Activity & Inflation

Lagarde has said there is no need for big ECB tightening because inflation should settle at target, per Yahoo Finance UK [[n1260]], although Al Jazeera reports she is no longer ruling out a hike this year. [[n1236]] Price pressure is broadening: Eurostat flagged rising euro-area energy prices in 2021 [[n1305]], Dutch inflation has reached its highest point in 40 years, per IamExpat [[n1309]], and UK motorists face record fuel prices, per the Guardian. [[n1996]] The Bank of England has hiked for a second time while the ECB stays put, per Barron's [[n1232]], and the ONS has published its first estimate of UK GDP for October to December. [[n1542]]
New / Most Important

Dutch TTF gas, the key transmission channel, rose 4.13% on Friday to 77.43 EUR/MWh, though it is still 9.40% below its level 20 sessions earlier, while the STOXX 600 slipped 0.59% to 469.57 index points and the Euro Stoxx 50 fell 1.00% to 4,155.23 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The EIA notes Europe relies primarily on imports to meet its natural gas needs. [[n1986]] The UK is the relative refuge: the FTSE 100 held at 7,661.00 index points, down just 0.15% on the day and up 1.56% over 20 sessions, as BP rose 1.58% and Shell 1.02% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer FTSE 100 exposure over the Euro Stoxx 50, whose US-listed ETF (FEZ) fell 2.71% on Friday, until gas risk is priced out (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger to deepen the underweight: TTF reclaiming its 20-session reference of 85.46 EUR/MWh. What changes the call: an ECB signal that it would lean against spread widening, or a diplomatic de-escalation that pushes TTF lower while growth holds.

geo.label: Easing into a property drag
parts: Macro Stance

China is the one major economy easing while the Fed tightens, and that divergence is the core of our Mixed stance. Bloomberg describes the PBOC as seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes [[n0141]], after it cut key lending rates, including one for the first time in nearly two years, according to CNBC. [[n0136]] The easing is starting to show up in credit, but it has not yet repaired the property chain or the consumer, and exporters face a more hostile trade backdrop. Investors are being asked to trust a policy pivot before the activity data confirm it.
PMIs & Activity

The latest factory read was soft: the Caixin PMI showed January activity contracting as Covid lockdowns bit, per Reuters. [[n0146]] That follows a strong 2021 base, with GDP growth of 8.1%, the fastest in a decade, as Global Times reported [[n0130]], and fixed-asset investment up 4.9% in 2021, according to Macau Business. [[n0132]] China Daily reports industrial profits rebounded in 2021 as production improved. [[n0144]] Consumption is the weak leg: CNBC reports the holiday box office plunged 23% as theaters pushed prices to record highs. [[n0171]] On the supply side, Reuters says China plans to increase iron ore output and boost steel-scrap use [[n0024]], a sign Beijing wants to contain input costs for the infrastructure push that China Briefing describes as the growth lever for 2022. [[n0236]]
Credit Impulse

The clearest early win for the easing camp is credit. Reuters reports Chinese government bond yields rose on faster January credit growth [[n0214]], which is the bond market saying it believes the impulse is turning. Lower policy rates reinforce that, with Fibre2Fashion noting cuts to medium-term lending and reverse repo rates. [[n0139]] The mechanism matters for global assets: a rising Chinese credit impulse tends to support Asian cyclicals and industrial commodities with a lag, but this cycle the property sector is where much of the new credit needs to land, and developers' capacity to absorb it is impaired.
Property

Property remains the drag that keeps us from turning Bullish. Reuters reports regulators are giving developers easier access to escrowed presale funds [[n0213]], a targeted liquidity release rather than a bailout. Evergrande says it aims to deliver 600,000 apartments in 2022 with no fire sales, per Reuters [[n0202]], while the WSJ reports its CEO sold bonds before the profit warning [[n0220]], a reminder that bondholder trust is broken. Nikkei Asia's reporting on concrete 'ghost towns' underlines the inventory overhang [[n0201]], and in Hong Kong lived-in home valuations are dropping amid a fifth Covid wave, per the South China Morning Post. [[n0178]] Business Recorder reported in January that new home prices fell less in December on promotions and easing curbs [[n0127]], so price stabilization is being bought with discounts. Escrow relief buys time; it does not create buyers.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Trade policy is turning more coercive in both directions. China suspended Lithuanian beef, dairy and beer imports as the Taiwan row grows, per Reuters [[n0216]], and Taiwan, Canada and Japan have asked to join the EU's WTO case against China, according to Politico Europe. [[n1457]] The Phase One relationship is souring too: the Peterson Institute calculates China bought none of the extra $200 billion of US exports in the Trump-era trade deal. [[n0169]] Domestically, oversight keeps tightening, with Reuters reporting a fine for Ant-backed MYBank over credit-scoring rules. [[n0151]] On Russia, The Hill argues China is making sanctions irrelevant [[n1443]], a stance that could raise secondary-sanctions risk for Chinese banks and exporters.
Markets & Flows

Onshore and offshore markets are telling different stories. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,462.95 index points, down 0.66% on Friday and up 3.02% over five sessions, a window that reaches back before the Lunar New Year closure, but still 3.26% lower over 20 sessions; the Hang Seng finished at 24,906.66 index points, 4.92% higher over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). In New York the China A-shares ETF (ASHR) fell 1.93% and the China internet ETF (KWEB) 3.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Regulatory risk remains sharp and idiosyncratic: WuXi Biologics sank by a record after landing on a US red-flag list, per the SCMP. [[n0177]] The SCMP's Macroscope column argues emerging markets are the ones to watch as tech-led US stocks lose their shine. [[n0250]]
New / Most Important

Technology self-sufficiency is the most important new strand. China's biggest chipmaker SMIC posted record revenue despite US sanctions, per CNBC [[n1175]], and plans to boost capacity after doubling profits to US$1.7 billion, according to the SCMP. [[n0243]] At the same time ASML has flagged possible IP infringement by a Chinese 'little giant', per the SCMP [[n0208]], which the Chinese company denies, according to Reuters. [[n0768]] Nikkei Asia reports ZTE is boosting its chip capabilities amid Huawei's crackdown woes. [[n0199]] Foreign capital is still committing to the premium consumer: BMW paid $4.2 billion to take control of its Chinese joint venture, Reuters reports. [[n0763]] Capital is flowing toward strategic self-sufficiency and premium consumption rather than the old property-led model.
Playbook ✓

Action: keep China at neutral, expressed through Hong Kong-listed platforms such as Tencent (453.04 HKD, up 6.84% over 20 sessions) rather than the A-share ETF (ASHR, down 4.07% over 20 sessions) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger to upgrade: a second month of accelerating credit growth alongside a factory PMI back in expansion. What changes the call: new US listing or sanctions actions against Chinese firms, or an escrow scheme that fails to stop developer defaults. ⚠ Divergence: bond yields are rising on faster credit growth, which normally signals reflation, yet the Caixin factory gauge is contracting and holiday spending is weak; the credit impulse has not yet reached activity.

geo.label: BOJ anchored, autos chip-constrained
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is the least exposed major market to the Fed shock through policy, and among the most exposed through industry. The BOJ still applies a negative rate to some bank deposits, including MUFG Bank's, per the Asahi Shimbun [[n1517]], and Reuters reported in January that it was debating how to message an eventual rate hike as inflation perks up. [[n1508]] Tokyo was shut for a holiday on Friday, so the Nikkei 225's last close of 27,696.08 index points, up 0.42%, predates the US risk-off (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). We are Mixed: policy is a cushion, but the export sector is chip-constrained.
Activity & Currency

The industrial picture is a chip story. Toyota's profits fell as production was hit, per the BBC [[n0550]], and the Japan Times argues that after a tough 2021 the outlook for Japanese carmakers is now down to chips. [[n1154]] Nissan raised its profit outlook but sees chips limiting growth, according to Reuters. [[n1086]] Demand is not the constraint: Reuters reported in January that December exports and imports hit record highs by value as supply bottlenecks eased. [[n1510]] Toyota closed at 2,254.00 JPY, down 6.55% over 20 sessions, while chip-equipment makers Tokyo Electron (57,150.00 JPY) and Advantest (9,600.00 JPY) rose 1.82% and 2.78% in their last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). On the currency, the mechanics favor the dollar: with the US two-year at 1.50% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11) and Japanese wages not rising, as the Japan Times explains [[n1531]], rate differentials keep widening, and the DXY is 1.36% firmer over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight Japanese chip-equipment names into the reopening, because the US-listed Japan ETF (EWJ) fell 0.81% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 4.83% in a session Tokyo missed (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger: Tokyo Electron failing to hold its last-session gain would confirm the catch-down. What changes the call: evidence that chip supply is easing for carmakers, or a BOJ signal of normalization that would remove the rate-differential tailwind for exporters.

geo.label: RBA patient as QE ends
parts: Macro Stance

Australia combines strong domestic data with a central bank that wants more proof before hiking. The SMH reports Australia is ending QE with a murky future for $650b of assets [[n0053]], following the RBA's February policy statement. [[n0016]] Inflation hit 3.5%, per the AFR [[n0009]], and the jobless rate is at a 13-year low, per The Australian. [[n0004]] We are Mixed: the data argue for hikes sooner than the RBA signals.
Demand & Financing

Credit demand is still driven by housing. CBA reported a first-half profit surge on the home boom and unveiled a share buyback, per Reuters [[n0033]], and The Australian says the bank is bullish on the economy as rate hikes loom. [[n0512]] The AFR flags rising rents as a sleeper factor for inflation [[n0060]], and the reopening of borders to vaccinated tourists on February 21 adds a services impulse, per Al Jazeera. [[n0022]] Supply remains a bottleneck, with Al Jazeera also reporting that border limbo in the mining state is sparking production fears. [[n0066]] Markets were softer on Friday: the S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.98% to 7,217.30 index points and CBA lost 2.21% to 98.55 AUD, while CSL is down 11.79% over 20 sessions and BHP gained 1.20% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer the iron ore miners, with Fortescue up 6.98% over five sessions and Rio Tinto up 2.86% on Friday, over the banks while the RBA keeps its patient line (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger: a hawkish shift in RBA language after the next wage or inflation print. What changes the call: China's plan to raise domestic iron ore output, reported by Reuters [[n0024]], turning into weaker seaborne demand, or a faster RBA pivot that slows bank loan growth.

geo.label: NBP hawkish on the front line
parts: Macro Stance

Poland combines the most hawkish central bank in our coverage with the most direct exposure to the Russia–Ukraine risk, which is why we are Mixed rather than outright Bearish. The Monetary Policy Council (RPP) raised rates again, taking them to their highest level in almost nine years, according to Rzeczpospolita. [[n1683]] NBP Governor Adam Glapiński framed his press conference around being a hawk ('Ja jako jastrząb', or 'Me as a hawk'), Interia reported [[n1697]], and Bankier credited him with strengthening the zloty [[n1720]], which it later described as the strongest in eight months. [[n1746]] The inflation problem behind that stance is real: GUS put end-2021 inflation at 8.6%, per 300Gospodarka [[n1595]], and Credit Agricole has raised its 2022 forecast to 7.5%, per Bankier. [[n1598]] The labour market keeps the pressure on, with average pay up 9.6% in 2021, per pb.pl [[n1722]], and registered unemployment at 5.6% in January, per Radio Maryja citing the family and social policy ministry (MRiPS). [[n1615]]
Markets

Warsaw has lagged the hawkish story. The iShares MSCI Poland ETF (EPOL) fell 3.88% on Friday to 20.31 USD and is down 10.96% over 20 sessions, while the WIG20 total-return tracker lost only 0.55% to 37.94 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The gap reflects mechanics: EPOL trades in dollars during New York hours, so it absorbs both currency translation and late-session US news, whereas the Warsaw close comes earlier in the day. Banks, the natural beneficiaries of higher rates, were heavy: Bank Pekao fell 2.24% to 133.15 PLN and PKO Bank Polski 1.04% to 47.65 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Parkiet still argues bank shares on the GPW have the potential to extend their bull run [[n1752]], while Bankier asks whether the market is still in a correction or already in a bear market. [[n1738]]
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal numbers are better than feared, but the politics are messier. The finance ministry estimates the 2021 state budget deficit at 26.3 bn zł, per Bankier [[n1776]], and Rzeczpospolita argues inflation is helping the government manage the public debt. [[n1623]] The Polski Ład tax reform has become a liability: deputy finance minister Jan Sarnowski, who was responsible for it, has lost his post, according to Business Insider Polska [[n1775]], a dismissal PolsatNews ties to the problems with Polski Ład [[n1772]], and Wyborcza.biz reports the next finance minister will be a woman. [[n1679]] Spending pressure is building, with pension indexation set to cost more than the budget assumed because of a higher index, per 300Gospodarka. [[n1787]] The food VAT cut is a double-edged tool that Credit Agricole says will contribute to higher inflation, per Bankier. [[n1591]] Relations with Brussels remain strained, with the EU set to withhold funds over the coal mine dispute, per DW. [[n1562]]
Corporate & Sectors

Corporate news is dominated by energy security and state champions. Orlen's CEO says jobs at Lotos will be maintained, per Bankier [[n1682]], and INNPoland reports Orlen has raised its wholesale petrol price, with stations unwilling to absorb the increase. [[n1674]] KGHM has registered its copper cathodes on China's INE exchange, according to Inwestycje.pl [[n1672]], and Parkiet reports Jacek Sasin and KGHM are travelling to the US in pursuit of small nuclear reactors. [[n1811]] Utilities are positioning for transition and rates: netka.gda.pl reports PGE's Baltica 3 offshore wind farm, of about 1045 MW, is planned to start in 2026 [[n1810]], and WNP.PL reports Tauron bought CO2 allowances at 30 euro and locked in a fixed interest rate. [[n1730]] In consumer names, LPP is optimistic about the year but expects cost pressure to weigh on margins, per Bankier. [[n1630]] Prices show the split: the coking-coal miner JSW is up 20.74% over 20 sessions and KGHM 9.44% over five, while Dino Polska is down 20.29% and Allegro 18.62% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Geopolitics & Security

Poland is now the staging ground for NATO reinforcement. Reuters reported exclusively that the US will send 3,000 additional troops to Poland [[n1586]], with ABC News reporting the 82nd Airborne deployment amid invasion concerns [[n1577]], and Politico Europe reports the UK is sending 350 more troops to the Polish border. [[n1557]] TVN24 describes further military transports arriving as proof that threats are being taken seriously [[n1801]], and Prime Minister Morawiecki has praised the UK's solidarity with Ukraine, Poland and NATO's eastern flank, per gov.pl. [[n1760]] Defence24 reports that Polish-made Piorun MANPADS have been exported to the US and provided to Ukraine, a commercial success for Mesko. [[n1582]] Energy is the economic channel: Money.pl reports businesses have received letters warning of gas-supply restrictions [[n1756]], and a survey reported by Bankier finds Europeans fear Russia will attack Ukraine this year. [[n1702]]
New / Most Important

The most important new signal is the NBP's reserve strategy. Business Insider Polska reports Glapiński intends to buy another 100 tonnes of gold [[n1699]], and Obserwator Gospodarczy calculates Poland could hold larger gold reserves than the UK or Saudi Arabia within a year. [[n1805]] Combined with Glapiński's pledge to keep urging tighter monetary policy, reported by PolsatNews [[n1723]], the message is that the NBP is building a war chest and is prepared to defend real rates and the currency. The Stowarzyszenie Inwestorów Indywidualnych reads the latest hike as a sign the NBP has not yet said its last word. [[n1688]] For markets, that lowers the probability of a disorderly currency sell-off even if the security situation deteriorates.
Playbook ✓

Action: hold Polish banks, PKO Bank Polski and Bank Pekao, as the rate-sensitive expression, fund them by underweighting the broad EPOL ETF until the Ukraine risk clears, and use JSW and KGHM as the commodity hedge. Trigger to add: another RPP hike with the currency's strength intact and EPOL stabilizing above its Friday close of 20.31 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). What changes the call: a Russian invasion that forces a flight from frontline assets, or fiscal slippage as Polski Ład repairs and pension costs pile up. ⚠ Divergence: the NBP is hawkish and Bankier reported the zloty at its strongest in eight months [[n1746]], which should support local assets, yet EPOL is down 10.96% over 20 sessions and bank shares sold off on Friday; the currency and the equity market are pricing different risks.
Narrative

Technology is where the bear flattening bites hardest, because long-dated cash flows are now discounted off a rising front end. XLK fell 3.05% on Friday to 154.89 USD and is down 5.77% over 20 sessions, with Adobe off 4.25% and Salesforce 4.49% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported

Fundamentals are not the problem. Tom's Hardware reports AMD set an all-time CPU market-share record [[n0497]], and the WSJ says Microsoft is keeping its finance head count flat with AI and bots. [[n1158]] The market is simply paying less for the same growth.
EPS Upside Watch

Consolidation is the upside lever. The WSJ reports Cisco made a takeover offer of more than $20 billion for Splunk [[n1178]], and Bloomberg says Microsoft is considering a deal for Mandiant. [[n0433]] Cash-rich acquirers can buy growth at compressed multiples, which favors large platforms over unprofitable software.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Apple's new way to pay by tapping iPhones together, per CNBC [[n1067]], shows the platforms moving into payments just as fintech multiples compress; Apple has held up better than peers, down 2.06% over 20 sessions to 168.64 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Narrative

Communication services has become the market's referendum on digital advertising. XLC fell 2.16% to 69.31 USD and is down 9.05% over 20 sessions, with Meta Platforms (FB) down 32.75% and Netflix 24.63% over the same span, and Alphabet fell 3.13% on Friday to 2,685.65 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported

Meta's fourth-quarter release triggered the steepest leg of the slide, with CNET reporting the shares plummeted on disappointing earnings and a user drop. [[n1026]] Disney is the counterexample: Variety reports Disney Plus ended 2021 with nearly 130 million subscribers, smashing growth forecasts [[n0529]], and Walt Disney is up 5.25% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
EPS Upside Watch

Capital return is the near-term lever: Twitter swung to a gain after announcing a new $4 billion buyback despite underwhelming user growth, per MarketWatch. [[n0714]] The Discovery–WarnerMedia deal has cleared US antitrust review, Reuters reports [[n0525]], setting up cost synergies for the combined streamer.
⚡ Breaking Convention
Forbes puts the impact of Apple's privacy changes on Meta at $10 billion [[n0638]], a reminder that platform rules, more than the ad cycle, now set earnings power in this sector.
Narrative

Financials should benefit from higher rates, but a flattening curve and a risk-off tape cap the upside. XLF fell 1.40% to 40.11 USD; JPMorgan Chase is down 8.51% and Goldman Sachs 7.10% over 20 sessions while Wells Fargo is up 4.13%, and the regional bank ETF (KRE) is down 4.99% as Charles Schwab fell 4.03% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported
Alternative managers are delivering: Forbes reports a record-breaking year at Apollo [[n0822]], and the WSJ says KKR's earnings fell while cash available to shareholders hit new heights. [[n0423]]
EPS Upside Watch

Net interest margin is the swing factor. A Kansas City Fed study examines whether margins at small and large banks respond differently to rates [[n2196]]; with the two-year up 59 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11), asset-sensitive lenders should see the first lift.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Sanctions are a hidden cost: Global Trade Review warns banks face a compliance 'nightmare' over looming Russia sanctions [[n1414]]. Meanwhile American Express is launching its first digital checking account, per CNBC [[n0379]], pushing a card network onto deposit turf.
Narrative

Energy is the market's cleanest hedge against both inflation and war. Brent rose 3.31% to 94.44 USD/bbl and WTI 3.58% to 93.10 USD/bbl, and XLE gained 2.91% to 70.41 USD, up 11.71% over 20 sessions, while Shell is up 12.00% over 20 sessions at 2,039.00 GBp (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported

Profits validate the move: Reuters says energy prices lifted BP's profits to an eight-year high [[n0408]], and the Borneo Bulletin reports TotalEnergies has returned to profit. [[n1192]] Equinor has published its fourth-quarter and year-end results. [[n0544]] Occidental Petroleum is up 25.86% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
EPS Upside Watch

The IEA has published its February Oil Market Report [[n0108]], and Reuters commentary calls diesel the US economy's inflation canary. [[n2183]] If middle distillates stay tight, refining margins benefit alongside upstream cash flow.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Shorts are leaning against the rally, per Barron's list of seven energy stocks with bearish bets [[n0751]], while AskTraders notes XLE has surged 23.2% in 2022. [[n0830]] Crowded skepticism into a war premium is fuel rather than friction; the bigger risk is the windfall-tax debate the BBC explains. [[n1102]]
Narrative

Industrials have split into defense winners and cyclical losers. XLI fell 1.53% to 99.36 USD and is down 6.70% over 20 sessions, yet Lockheed Martin is up 8.49% over that span and Northrop Grumman rose 4.53% on Friday, while Caterpillar is down 11.35% and Eaton 11.99% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported
Maersk reported record earnings for 2021 with profit up triple, per the Indonesia Shipping Gazette [[n0565]], while Reuters says Boeing deliveries remain low as 787 problems weigh. [[n0390]]
EPS Upside Watch

Regulation is reshaping defense portfolios: CNBC reports Lockheed Martin terminated its $4.4 billion deal for Aerojet Rocketdyne amid regulatory roadblocks [[n0887]], and Reuters reports Raytheon Technologies (RTX) says it is a target of a DOJ probe into industry hiring practices. [[n0810]]
⚡ Breaking Convention

Airline consolidation is back, with Frontier buying Spirit Airlines in a $2.9 billion budget-carrier deal, per Reuters [[n0296]], an unusual bet on scale as fuel costs climb. Reuters also reports FedEx is eyeing a freighter order as e-commerce soars [[n0412]], so cargo capacity, rather than passenger traffic, is where airframe demand looks firm.
Narrative

Discretionary spending faces a real-income squeeze and a confidence shock at once. XLY fell 2.87% to 180.48 USD and is down 8.59% over 20 sessions, with Tesla down 16.63% and Home Depot 9.48% over that span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), and Yahoo Finance says US consumers are 'in a deep funk'. [[n2147]]
Reported

Restaurants are passing costs through: CBS News reports Chipotle plans to hike menu prices again [[n1176]], after record profit, per MarketWatch. [[n0519]] Harley-Davidson's results topped forecasts as motorcycle demand soared, according to Reuters [[n1074]], and Reuters says Yum Brands' sales were boosted by demand for tacos and fried chicken. [[n0558]]
EPS Upside Watch

Peloton's reset under a new CEO, with about 2,800 job cuts reported by Business Insider [[n0442]], shows margin repair is the lever left for pandemic winners; the stock is still up 40.98% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) after the BBC relayed reports that Amazon and Nike were exploring a takeover. [[n0265]]
⚡ Breaking Convention
Tesla's recall of over 500,000 US vehicles to fix pedestrian warning sounds, per Reuters [[n1968]], is a reminder that software risk now sits inside auto valuations.
Narrative

Staples are being tested on pricing power, not demand. XLP slipped 0.36% to 75.25 USD on Friday and is down only 2.13% over 20 sessions, against a 5.16% fall for the S&P 500, and Nestle rose 1.07% to 119.28 CHF on Friday, a sign of a defensive bid for pricing power (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported

Coca-Cola beat estimates as demand for drinks away from home topped pre-pandemic levels, per CNBC [[n0650]], but Reuters reports Coca-Cola and PepsiCo both warned of an inflation bite even as higher prices lifted sales. [[n0651]] Reuters also says inflation is turning up the heat on Unilever. [[n0673]]
EPS Upside Watch

Kellogg joins Chipotle and Starbucks in planning price hikes this year, per Forbes [[n1155]], even as its labor strike eats into margins, according to Reuters. [[n0559]] The test is whether volumes hold through a second round of increases.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Membership models are monetizing loyalty: Good Morning America examines how Costco and grocery membership fee hikes affect buying decisions [[n0670]]; Costco fell 1.70% on Friday to 509.67 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Narrative

Health care is defensive in theory, but the Covid revenue cliff is splitting the sector. XLV fell 1.39% to 130.25 USD; AbbVie is up 6.36% over 20 sessions while Moderna is down 23.24% and Pfizer 8.57% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported

Pfizer's vaccine and pill forecasts missed estimates and the shares fell 4%, per The Peninsula Qatar [[n0449]], and Reuters reports CVS forecast its Covid vaccine business could drop by up to 80% in 2022. [[n0513]] AstraZeneca, by contrast, sees higher 2022 sales even as the Covid boost wanes, according to Reuters. [[n1946]]
EPS Upside Watch

Capital return and pipelines carry the next leg: Amgen will buy back $6 billion of shares this quarter, per Reuters [[n0382]], and MedPage Today reports Lilly's tirzepatide won as an add-on to insulin glargine. [[n1901]]
⚡ Breaking Convention

BioPharma Dive reports the biotech rout has left drug startups grounded as demand slumps for IPOs [[n1346]]; the biotech ETF (XBI) is down 4.84% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Large caps still have deal capacity: Fierce Pharma reports Lilly is back in the Covid antibody game with a $720M US deal for an omicron-busting candidate. [[n0793]]
Narrative

Materials are a tale of commodity leaders and a lagging sector ETF. Aluminum futures are up 11.49% over 20 sessions at 3,282.25 USD/t, Alcoa 21.50% and CF Industries 17.02%, yet XLB is down 6.21% over the same period at 84.00 USD and Freeport-McMoRan 3.45% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported

DuPont beat profit estimates on price hikes and electronics demand, per Reuters [[n0404]], and ArcelorMittal has published its fourth-quarter and full-year 2021 results. [[n1142]] RNZ reports Rio Tinto wants to keep operating the Tiwai Point smelter past its 2024 closure date [[n0451]], suggesting aluminium economics now justify keeping capacity open.
EPS Upside Watch

Fertilizer is the upside pocket: the USDA says fertilizer prices spiked in late 2021 just ahead of the planting season [[n1920]], and Mosaic is up 12.64% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Reuters columnist Andy Home notes a surge in LME stocks has failed to cool the red-hot aluminium market. [[n0211]]
⚡ Breaking Convention

Gold miners are consolidating while bullion is bid: Agnico Eagle and Kirkland Lake Gold have sealed their deal, per Northern Ontario Business [[n0502]], and Newmont rose 5.50% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Narrative

Real estate is the most direct casualty of the front-end repricing. XLRE fell 1.37% to 45.42 USD and is down 7.04% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), as financing costs reset higher, with the Orange County Register putting the 30-year mortgage rate at 3.69%. [[n2135]]
Reported
Realtor.com reports mortgage rates surged to their highest point since Jan. 2020 [[n2134]], and the WSJ says Zillow's shuttered home-flipping business lost $881 million in 2021. [[n0735]]
EPS Upside Watch

Supply scarcity is the offset: Realtor.com finds the US housing supply gap expanded in 2021 [[n2114]], and a real estate investor tells Barron's that housing isn't a bubble, offices aren't dead and malls can thrive. [[n0784]] Owners of scarce, well-located assets can still push rents.
⚡ Breaking Convention

HousingWire asks whether it is really the worst time ever to buy a house in the US [[n2123]]; when affordability rather than demand is the constraint, rental landlords gain at the expense of transaction-driven businesses. CNN reports household debt jumped by $1 trillion in 2021, the most since 2007 [[n2108]], so leverage is already elevated going into the rate cycle.
Narrative

Utilities were the rare sector that held flat on Friday, with XLU up 0.06% to 67.03 USD, but they are still down 4.08% over 20 sessions because higher yields compete with their dividends; Southern Company rose 1.27% on Friday while Duke Energy is down 4.32% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported

Duke Energy plans to exit all coal and double renewables, per E&E News [[n0775]], having expanded its clean energy action plan, per its news center [[n0540]], while NextEra Energy is down 11.71% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), showing that growth-utility multiples are rate-sensitive.
EPS Upside Watch

Barron's calls Berkshire Hathaway's utility business a crown jewel [[n0356]], and KWQC reports Exelon has completed its separation from Constellation [[n0289]], sharpening the investor choice between regulated and merchant power.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Fuel costs cut both ways: Reuters reports Japanese utilities are reeling as sky-high fuel prices hit earnings [[n0999]], a warning for any utility that cannot pass through gas costs to customers. France's renewed commitment to new reactors, reported by Reuters [[n1958]], keeps nuclear baseload in the European utility debate.
Narrative

European autos are rallying on pricing power just as the region's war risk rises. The STOXX 600 autos tracker (EXV5.DE) rose 0.94% to 62.29 EUR on Friday and 5.10% over five sessions, though it remains 5.16% lower over 20 sessions; Volkswagen preference shares rose 7.10% over five sessions while Renault fell 1.53% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported

Mercedes-Benz Group beat its profit forecast but sees supply-chain headwinds in 2022, per Reuters [[n0797]], and Bloomberg says Mercedes cars are more profitable than ever amid the chip shortage. [[n1182]] BMW gained 2.73% to 95.30 EUR on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
EPS Upside Watch

Reuters reports the Mercedes-Benz CFO sees an easing of supply-chain woes in the second half [[n0796]], and ACEA expects EU car sales to rise 7.9% in 2022 as chip supply stabilises, per Reuters. [[n1861]] Volume recovery on top of record pricing is the upside case.
⚡ Breaking Convention
The competitive threat is arriving from China: Xpeng will open its first retail store in Europe, per CNBC [[n0647]], and is expanding into Sweden and the Netherlands, according to Reuters. [[n0648]]
Narrative

Semiconductors led Friday's decline. The PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 4.83% to 3,365.25 index points and SOXX 5.09% to 464.02 USD, down 11.22% over 20 sessions; Advanced Micro Devices lost 10.01%, Nvidia 7.26% and ASML's US line 4.36% to 628.24 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported

Strategic deals are unwinding: Nvidia and SoftBank Group announced the termination of Nvidia's acquisition of Arm, per the NVIDIA Newsroom [[n1053]], and Reuters reports SoftBank will take Arm to an IPO instead. [[n0458]] TSMC's ADR is down 13.06% over 20 sessions at 121.01 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
EPS Upside Watch

Policy support is building in Europe, where ASML says it supports the European Chip Act proposal, per Reuters. [[n0370]] Memory is the relative bright spot, with SK Hynix up 6.02% and Micron Technology 10.58% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Intel is launching a blockchain chip to tap the crypto boom, per Reuters [[n0789]], and a $1 billion fund to build a foundry innovation ecosystem, per its investor relations site [[n1869]], betting on new demand pools rather than PC share.

earnings_pattern.title: Pricing power paid, guidance gaps punished
parts: Rewarded

The market is paying for pricing power and visible cash return. Mercedes-Benz Group jumped 6.72% on Friday to 74.44 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) after beating its profit forecast, per Reuters. [[n0797]] GeekWire reports Zillow shares rose 16% on its 'housing super app' strategy amid the iBuying closure [[n0734]], and Reuters says Disney+ streaming growth and park revenue boosted Disney's shares. [[n0532]] Bloom Energy rose 8.97% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) after publishing its fourth-quarter results and long-term growth update. [[n0645]]
Punished

Growth stories with soft outlooks are being sold hard. Affirm fell 20.67% to 46.55 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) after results that PYMNTS says shine a light on merchant take-rate tradeoffs. [[n0754]] Uber is down 4.75% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) after its 2024 profit forecast fell short of expectations, per Reuters. [[n0717]] CNBC reports Delivery Hero's CEO apologized after a 30% stock plunge [[n0774]], and Reuters says Lyft's weak rider numbers outweighed its first full-year profit. [[n0426]]
Pattern

The common thread is duration. With the two-year up 59 bps in 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11), investors discount distant profits more heavily and reward companies that can lift prices or shrink their share count now. BP is the template: AJ Bell argues falling debt helps explain its rising share price [[n0779]], and BP rose 1.58% to 417.20 GBp on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). A beat is not enough when costs threaten margins: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo both warned of an inflation bite, per Reuters [[n0651]], and Coca-Cola fell 1.78% on Friday.
Attention into EPS

Attention now shifts to whether cost inflation reaches margins in the next round of reports. Early reporters are diverging: The Toy Book reports Hasbro revenue spiked 17% in 2021 [[n1050]], Shimano hit record revenue and earnings in its centennial year, per Bicycle Retailer [[n1081]], while Thomson Reuters missed on earnings but set higher revenue goals, according to Reuters. [[n1098]] DuPont's beat on price hikes, per Reuters [[n0404]], is the model the market wants to see repeated.
Playbook

Action: buy results that combine a beat with pricing or buybacks on the first pullback, and fade beats that rely on volume while warning on costs. Trigger: a stock that holds its post-results gain while the VIX stays above 27.36 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) has demonstrated real sponsorship. What changes the call: if the two-year stops rising, the punished long-duration names become short-squeeze candidates and the pricing-power premium compresses.

underowned.title: Fertilizer and the grain chain
parts: Attention Gap

While attention is on tech drawdowns, the crop-input chain has quietly repriced. CF Industries is up 17.02% and Mosaic 12.64% over 20 sessions, with CBOT wheat at 797.75 US cents/bu and soybeans at 1,583.00 US cents/bu (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Exposure & Risk

The USDA says fertilizer prices spiked in late 2021 ahead of planting [[n1920]], Successful Farming reports soybeans closed near $16 per bushel [[n1929]], and Farm Progress lists three reasons wheat could be this year's big winner. [[n1943]] The risk is demand destruction if input costs force farmers to cut application rates.
Trigger to Watch

A Black Sea disruption, which Ukraine already accuses Russia of escalating, per the Atlantic Council [[n1440]], would tighten grain supply; a diplomatic thaw would deflate the premium. Watch corn at 651.00 US cents/bu, up 10.81% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

underowned.title: The nuclear fuel cycle
parts: Attention Gap

Nuclear power is back on policy agendas without a matching investor rush. Reuters reports Macron is betting on nuclear in his carbon-neutrality push and announcing new reactors [[n1958]], and Global News reports Cameco will restart its McArthur River uranium mine. [[n0514]]
Exposure & Risk

Cameco rose 11.87% over five sessions to 22.25 USD and the uranium ETF (URA) 6.48%, but both are still lower over 20 sessions, by 3.22% and 5.86% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Supply restarts can cap prices before utilities sign contracts.
Trigger to Watch

Utility and reactor commitments are the trigger. Bankier reports TVA is putting $200 million into preparing a new US reactor [[n1813]], and Parkiet reports KGHM is pursuing small reactors in the US. [[n1811]] The uranium ETF, at 21.84 USD, remains the diversified expression (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

underowned.title: Gold miners as the war hedge
parts: Attention Gap

Gold miners are outperforming bullion on risk-off days. GDX rose 5.67% on Friday to 32.43 USD while front-month gold rose 0.26% to 1,842.10 USD/oz and GLD 1.91% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11); the gap between futures and the later-closing ETF suggests the bid intensified late in the session.
Exposure & Risk

Reuters reports gold jumped as rising Ukraine tensions spurred safe-haven demand [[n2209]], and the World Gold Council's John Reade has reviewed gold's recent performance. [[n2210]] Miners add operating leverage to bullion, along with cost-inflation risk.
Trigger to Watch

Official buying is a structural bid, with the NBP planning to buy another 100 tonnes, per Business Insider Polska [[n1699]], while the WGC says India's retail demand remained soft in January. [[n1830]] Watch whether GDX holds Friday's gain if diplomacy advances; a fade would show the move was positioning rather than a new allocation.

underowned.title: Hong Kong-listed China platforms
parts: Attention Gap

With US technology under pressure, Hong Kong's platforms have quietly outperformed. The Hang Seng is up 4.92% over 20 sessions while the Nasdaq 100 is down 8.01%, and Alibaba's Hong Kong line rose 0.16% on Friday to 122.40 HKD as its US ADR fell 1.40% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Exposure & Risk

The SCMP argues emerging markets are the ones to watch as tech-led US stocks lose their shine. [[n0250]] XPeng's inclusion in the Shenzhen–Hong Kong Stock Connect, announced by the company, widens the mainland buyer base for Hong Kong lines. [[n0484]] Regulation remains the main risk.
Trigger to Watch

The trigger is whether the Hang Seng holds above its 20-session reference of 23,739.06 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). A wider US red-flag list, which sent WuXi Biologics down by a record, per the SCMP [[n0177]], would reverse the trade.

crypto.title: Bitcoin trades as beta, not as a hedge
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed its latest UTC day at 42,197.52 USD, down 0.11%, 4.35% lower over five sessions but still 15.12% above its level 20 sessions earlier; Ether finished at 2,883.46 USD, down 7.66% over five sessions, and Solana fell 17.92% over five sessions to 93.24 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-13). The equity proxies did worse in Friday's risk-off: Coinbase Global fell 5.00% to 194.53 USD, MicroStrategy 4.74% and Marathon Digital 6.56% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The early-February rebound had taken Bitcoin to $44,000 after five straight gains, per Al Jazeera [[n0898]], before US inflation numbers dented the wider crypto recovery again, according to Gadgets 360. [[n0958]]
New / Most Important

Enforcement is the dominant story: the Justice Department seized $3.6 billion of bitcoin stolen in a crypto hack, per Barron's. [[n0422]] Regulation is fragmenting, with The Block reporting that a House hearing rejected the Treasury's proposed stablecoin regime [[n0926]], and Reuters saying Coinbase removed cryptocurrency links after 'rug pull' warnings. [[n0947]] Marketing has gone mainstream, with CBS News reporting crypto companies spending millions on Super Bowl advertising [[n0109]], and WIRED saying the pre-game crypto ads feel like Pets.com all over again. [[n0112]] Institutional plumbing keeps growing: Canada's TMX Group plans a crypto futures product for institutions, per Reuters [[n0919]], and KPMG in Canada has added Bitcoin and Ethereum to its corporate treasury. [[n0905]]
Playbook

Action: treat crypto as high-beta risk rather than a war hedge, because on Friday gold miners rallied while crypto equities fell; keep exposure small and prefer spot over leveraged miners. Trigger to add: Bitcoin reclaiming the $44,000 level it reached in early February. [[n0898]] What changes the call: a break below its 20-session reference of 36,654.33 USD would signal the January drawdown is resuming, while Bitcoin rising alongside a VIX above 27.36 index points would give the hedge narrative its first real evidence (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-13; Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

flows.title: Liquidity drains as money hides in yield
parts: Global Liquidity

Global liquidity is tightening from the top. Reuters commentary argues a historic central-bank drain is calling 'buy the dip' into question [[n1363]], and the Financial Times reports markets are losing trust in central banks. [[n1357]] The Fed pointed to a rate hike in March at its January meeting, per CNBC [[n2165]]; Business Insider reports the Bank of England has hiked again [[n1239]], and the SMH says Australia is ending QE. [[n0053]] The offset comes from the periphery: the FT notes emerging markets are signalling an end to aggressive rate-raising cycles [[n0083]], China is easing, and The Week reports the RBI kept its repo rate unchanged at 4%. [[n1364]] The net effect is a shrinking pool of marginal liquidity for long-duration assets, because the economies still adding liquidity are not the ones that set global discount rates.
Rates & Dollar

The front end is doing the work. The two-year sits at 1.50% after a 59 bps rise over 20 observations, while the 10Y−2Y spread has compressed 37 bps to +42 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11). NBC Connecticut had the ten-year at 1.96% with the inflation data in focus [[n1347]], and CNBC reports it then topped 2% for the first time since 2019 [[n2192]], before Friday's haven bid pulled it back to 1.92% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11). Mortgage News Daily summed up the backdrop as the highest inflation since the 80s, the highest rates since 2019 and huge volatility on Friday. [[n2211]] Treasuries still worked as a hedge on Friday: IEF rose 1.04%, TLT 1.48% and SHY 0.31%, while the dollar index is up 1.36% over 20 sessions at 96.08 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Morningstar examines why inflation-protected bond funds are losing money [[n1376]], a symptom of rising real yields.
Credit Check

Credit is softening, not breaking. The high-yield ETF (HYG) fell 0.35% on Friday and is down 4.07% over 20 sessions, investment-grade LQD rose 0.74% on the Treasury rally but is down 4.20% over 20 sessions, and the emerging-market bond ETF (EMB) is 3.31% lower (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). 9fin describes a paltry primary leveraged-finance market [[n1311]], and the Richmond Fed has examined how post-2008 regulation affected corporate bond liquidity [[n1361]], a reminder that dealer balance sheets are thin if selling accelerates. In China, the SCMP reports Evergrande's CEO dumped all his dollar bonds before default [[n0221]], keeping property credit stress concentrated in developers. Sanctions add an operational layer for lenders, with Global Trade Review warning banks face a compliance nightmare over looming Russia sanctions. [[n1414]]
Equity & Fund Flows

Measured flow evidence points to a rotation into income, not capitulation. Reuters reports US dividend funds received huge inflows as investors switched out of bonds [[n1360]], and the WSJ says investors are gobbling up dividend stocks during the turbulence. [[n0420]] At the speculative end, Cathie Wood's ARK is staying the course on innovation, per the WSJ [[n0882]], even as ARKK is down 10.10% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Primary markets are selective: Abu Dhabi Ports surged 15% in its debut after raising $1.1 billion, per CNBC [[n1348]], and India's Life Insurance Corporation has filed for an $8 billion IPO [[n1378]], while Reuters reports Atlantic Coastal's SPAC scrapped its merger with Essentium [[n1374]] and Syniverse and SPAC M3-Brigade scrapped a $2.85 billion merger. [[n1359]] Active managers are de-risking single names too: Bloomberg reports Cathie Wood dumped $142 million of Twitter stock before earnings. [[n0282]] In Korea, KED Global reports money flows rushing to safer assets. [[n1344]]
Portfolio Implication

Position for a liquidity regime that rewards cash flow today: overweight dividend payers and energy, hold IEF as the shock absorber, keep a gold allocation through GLD, which rose 1.91% on Friday, as the non-dollar hedge, and stay underweight long-duration growth and high yield. Trigger to rotate back toward risk: HYG stabilizing while the VIX retreats toward its 20-session reference of 20.31 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). What changes the call: Fed pushback against a half-point move, which the Fed's Barkin has signalled, per Reuters [[n1365]], combined with diplomacy. Even the sell side is split: Bloomberg reports JPMorgan strategists see a sure-fire sign it is time to buy stocks [[n0421]], while JPMorgan has also warned the tech sell-off may continue for another month, per The Edge Malaysia. [[n0310]]

anticipatory.title: Invasion or de-escalation: the binary for risk assets
parts: What Is Priced

Markets carry a partial war premium, not a full one: Brent at 94.44 USD/bbl, the VIX at 27.36 index points and gold miners up 5.67% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Washington is warning of war 'any day', per the Seychelles News Agency [[n1488]], with over 130,000 Russian troops staged outside Ukraine, according to PBS. [[n1497]]
Conditional Expression

If an invasion begins, the conditional expression is long crude, long defense through the aerospace and defense ETF (ITA, 105.18 USD) and long Treasuries, against European banks and EPOL (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). If diplomacy delivers de-escalation, fade the energy premium and buy back the Nasdaq 100's 8.01% 20-session drawdown. So far, Al Jazeera reports the Biden–Putin talks yielded no breakthrough. [[n1494]]
Risk

The risk is timing: a slow-burning standoff lets premia bleed away before any resolution. Business Insider quotes a Black Swan fund manager on three events that could trigger a 20% crash [[n1498]], a reminder that tail hedges are cheap only before the event. Commercial activity is already repricing: Forbes reports KLM has suspended flights to Ukraine. [[n1489]]

anticipatory.title: March Fed: quarter point or big bang
parts: What Is Priced

The two-year at 1.50%, after a 59 bps jump over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11), already prices a fast cycle. Reuters reports hot inflation fuels the case for a 'big-bang' hike in March [[n2201]], a step beyond the January Reuters poll that expected three hikes this year. [[n2038]]
Conditional Expression

If the Fed opens the door to a half-point start, expect further bear flattening: stay short the front end through SHY and underweight real estate (XLRE). If it keeps to a quarter point with a firm path, the curve can re-steepen modestly and growth stocks get relief. CME Group's analysis of Fed rate hike expectations versus reality is a useful frame for comparing market pricing with delivered hikes [[n2170]], and Morningstar's charts on the CPI rise and the rate-hike outlook show the same tension. [[n2193]]
Risk

The risk is that a war shock forces the Fed to slow, or that inflation rolls over: Fortune argues high inflation is sticking around but likely peaked months ago. [[n2131]] Either would punish aggressive front-end shorts.

anticipatory.title: Sanctions design: energy carve-outs versus financial plumbing
parts: What Is Priced

TTF at 77.43 EUR/MWh is still 9.40% below its level 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), so the gas market is not pricing a supply cut. Reuters reports Biden has pledged an end to Nord Stream 2 if Russia invades Ukraine. [[n1241]]
Conditional Expression

If the immediate sanctions Scholz has warned of, per Reuters [[n1499]], target finance first, the pressure falls on lenders with eastern exposure and on payment rails; if they hit energy, TTF and European utilities move first. Senator Graham says the West is talking way too much and doing too little on sanctions, per Politico [[n1504]], so the package could be broader than markets assume; the Guardian reports Liz Truss also warned Russia of sanctions during tense talks. [[n1449]]
Risk

The risk is leakage. Reuters explains how a German 'climate' fund set out to help Russia dodge US sanctions [[n1325]], and The Hill argues China is making sanctions on Russia irrelevant. [[n1443]] Weak enforcement would cap the market impact.

anticipatory.title: Iran nuclear deal and the crude supply offset
parts: What Is Priced

Brent at 94.44 USD/bbl, with WTI up 13.37% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), embeds little additional Iranian supply. Reuters reports Iran's oil exports are increasing as nuclear talks resume [[n1437]], and Voice of America says the US sees the talks at an urgent point with a few weeks left to complete a deal. [[n1427]] France 24 reports Tehran calls the removal of US sanctions its 'red line' for reviving the 2015 nuclear deal. [[n1382]]
Conditional Expression

If a deal is reached, the conditional expression is to trim the highest-beta upstream names, with Occidental up 25.86% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), while keeping integrated majors. If talks collapse, crude carries both an Iran and a Russia premium. Axios reports Israel puts Iran's nuclear breakout time at 4–6 months with a deal [[n1420]], which shapes Washington's urgency.
Risk
The risk is political: Politico reports lawmakers are pessimistic about a new Iran deal [[n1434]], so a deal could stall even after negotiators agree.

catalysts.title: Mercedes-Benz Group (MBG.DE): pricing power through the chip squeeze
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Mercedes-Benz Group rose 6.72% on Friday to 74.44 EUR and 9.74% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) after Bloomberg reported its cars are more profitable than ever amid the chip shortage. [[n1182]] The thesis: a luxury mix lets it pass on costs while volumes are capped, and the CFO sees supply-chain woes easing in the second half, per Reuters. [[n0796]]
Price Hurdle & Risk

The hurdle is its 20-session reference of 74.79 EUR; the stock is still 0.47% below it (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The risk is a Ukraine escalation that hits European demand and energy costs at the same time.
Trade Expression
Long Mercedes-Benz Group against the Euro Stoxx 50 ETF (FEZ) to isolate pricing power from the regional war discount; cut the position if the stock gives back Friday's gain.

catalysts.title: Lockheed Martin (LMT): regulatory overhang lifted as demand rises
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Lockheed Martin terminated its $4.4 billion deal for Aerojet Rocketdyne amid regulatory roadblocks, per CNBC [[n0887]], removing a distraction just as the Washington Post reports the Pentagon is sending another 3,000 troops to Poland. [[n1581]] Defense demand looks set to rise, and the freed-up capital could go to buybacks or other deals.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Lockheed closed at 396.19 USD, up 2.79% on Friday and 8.49% over 20 sessions from 365.18 USD, while Northrop Grumman rose 4.53% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The risk is a diplomatic breakthrough that drains the war premium.
Trade Expression

Long Lockheed against Boeing, at 212.30 USD and down 5.18% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), to isolate defense from civil aerospace; reassess if defense names give back Friday's gains while Brent holds its premium.

catalysts.title: Exxon Mobil (XOM): earnings leverage to a war premium
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Exxon Mobil's fourth-quarter profit topped estimates as oil and gas prices soared, per CNBC [[n0993]], and Yahoo Finance reports it is expanding oil futures and products trading in Europe. [[n0778]] With Brent at 94.44 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), operating leverage favors the integrated majors, and Chevron is up 9.47% over 20 sessions.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Exxon closed at 80.21 USD, up 2.52% on Friday and 13.56% over 20 sessions, though down 1.47% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The risk is an Iran deal or a Russian de-escalation that drains the crude premium.
Trade Expression
Own Exxon outright, add if Brent holds above 94.44 USD/bbl, and trim on any credible Iran agreement; funding it from the Nasdaq 100 keeps the position a hedge rather than an extra beta bet.

catalysts.title: Meta Platforms (FB): regulation, privacy and a costly pivot
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Meta Platforms has said it may shut down Facebook and Instagram in Europe over a data-sharing dispute, per CNBC [[n1259]], and has renewed that warning to the EU, per Time. [[n0429]] CNBC also reports Peter Thiel is stepping down from its board. [[n0324]] CNBC notes its market cap has fallen below $600 billion, which could even help it dodge new antitrust scrutiny. [[n0409]]
Price Hurdle & Risk

Meta closed at 219.55 USD, down 3.74% on Friday, 7.40% over five sessions and 32.75% over 20 sessions from 326.48 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The risk to the short is that valuation alone attracts buyers.
Trade Expression
Stay underweight; what changes the call is a resolution of the EU data-sharing dispute that removes the European revenue risk.

catalysts.title: Nvidia (NVDA): Arm gone, rates up
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The Guardian reports Nvidia's $40bn takeover of Arm has collapsed [[n0438]], and WIRED says the collapse leaves Arm exposed. [[n1909]] CNBC asks whether the deal was doomed from the start. [[n0403]] Without the deal, Nvidia trades on its core growth multiple just as the front end reprices.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Nvidia closed at 239.49 USD, down 7.26% on Friday and 9.88% over 20 sessions from 265.75 USD, while the 3x semiconductor ETF (SOXL) fell 14.82% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The risk is a strong next print that resets the growth debate.
Trade Expression
Underweight Nvidia against Micron Technology, at 89.76 USD and up 10.58% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), to stay long memory pricing while short duration.

catalysts.title: Coca-Cola (KO): a beat that came with a warning
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Food Business News reports Coca-Cola is beginning to hit pre-pandemic volume levels [[n0769]], and CNBC says its earnings beat estimates. [[n0650]] But RTE reports both PepsiCo and Coke warned of the inflation impact [[n1164]], so the margin path depends on price acceptance.
Price Hurdle & Risk
